summary: On Windows without symlink privilege, tarfile silently extracts a copy of a symlink's target, so _verify_export refuses every candidate tree containing a mode-120000 entry.
failure_scenario: Windows host, os.symlink raises OSError -> tarfile.makelink_with_filter falls back to copying the target file -> observed entry is a regular file (mode 100644, different blob id) vs expected 120000 -> ContractViolation 'differs from the exact Git tree'. Legacy gates over any repo with a symlink (previously exported as copies) now fail closed on such hosts. Fail-closed, so not an authority hole, but a new compatibility regression with a misleading 'export-ignore/export-subst' message.
evidence: Read tarfile.makelink_with_filter source (copy fallback on symlink_exception) and the new _verify_export; no new test contains a symlink entry (grep of tests/substrate/test_git_authority.py and tests/e2e/test_legacy_gate_snapshot.py). Not executed on Windows.

summary: The export-ignore e2e test asserts only 'not SUCCEEDED / main unmoved / no EffectCommitted', so it would also pass if the run failed for an unrelated reason before reaching read_snapshot's verification.
failure_scenario: If propose or any earlier node fails (or the snapshot raises for a different reason), all four assertions still hold and the guard is never shown to have been reached; the unit tests in test_git_authority.py do pin the refusal message, but the composed path does not.
evidence: Read the test: no assertion on the failure reason/event kind or on ContractViolation text. Candidate record claims it fails with the source stashed, which I did not re-run. Composed focused tests pass on the assembled tree (122 passed).

summary: CheckResult now refuses a stored payload with status='passed' and a string ok that coerces to False, which the pre-fix validator accepted (as passed/ok=False).
